<security_assessment>

<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source download from the project's official GitHub releases: a `.deb` file for version 1.15.0 of "parallel-code". The `sha256sums` array contains a valid checksum, so the integrity of the downloaded binary artifact will be verified during source fetching.

During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, the only executed portions are the global scope and `pkgver()` (if present). This PKGBUILD has no `pkgver()` function, and no command substitutions or external executions in the global scope. The variables are all static or derived from static ones (like `_pkgname`). No code is executed as part of sourcing the PKGBUILD.

The source fetch involves a direct HTTPS download of a pinned release asset over a secure channel from the official upstream. There are no git operations, dynamic URL constructions, or remote code executions triggered during sourcing. The use of a prebuilt binary (`.deb`) with a proper checksum is acceptable for this safety gate. Extraction happens after download but remains inert due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`.

Thus, running the specified makepkg commands poses no risk of executing malicious payloads or exfiltrating data at parse/fetch time.
</details>
<evidence>
